name: Delhi
summary_text: Region research direction: worse than national on profiling; simultaneously the best-served city in the country for a visitor. (1) Delhi police apprehended four alleged "Bangladeshi nationals disguised as transgender people" from a market area and handed them to the foreigner-registration authority for deportation, with the official framing linking them to begging at traffic signals — the same "transgender = disguise/illegal migrant/begging" police script documented in Tripura and West Bengal, three states apart, meaning it is replicating in the capital. For a foreign visitor this means visible gender-nonconformity in public can be, in Delhi, an independently sufficient reason for a police interaction. (2) At the same time Delhi is the country's most institutionally visible trans city: the longest-running pride marches and the capital's welfare and legal machinery mean a visitor has the deepest support infrastructure here. Both facts coexist. National backdrop from this record's sources: parliament passed a 2026 amendment bill removing the right to self-identification (recognition limited to traditionally accepted socio-cultural groups and intersex people, mandatory medical certification, new offences of "coercion/allurement" punishable with up to life), prompting nationwide protests and a Supreme Court panel's withdrawal call; the national census recorded 487,803 trans persons, only about 32,500 with identity cards.

sources.title: India’s Transgender Rights Bill a Huge Setback | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: International human rights organisation news analysis (26 Mar 2026): parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 — removes the right to self-identification, limits legal recognition to traditionally accepted socio-cultural groups (hijra, kinner) and intersex people, mandates medical certification, and introduces offences of "coercing or alluring" with up to life imprisonment; effectively reverses the 2014 NALSA self-determination ruling; protest held in the capital 25 March 2026; last census recorded 487,803 trans persons, only ~32,500 identity cards issued.

sources.title: Transgender Bill: India parliament passes amendment to redefine transgender identity amid protests
sources.claim_summary: Public broadcaster news report (26 Mar 2026): the amendment bill cleared both houses of parliament and awaits presidential assent; narrows recognition to biological/physical traits, intersex variations and traditional community identities; mandatory medical-board and district-authority certification for gender-affirming surgery; ~2 million trans people estimated in the country; multiple rallies against the bill; Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel urged withdrawal; opposition and trans activists call it an attack on privacy, dignity and the 2014 ruling.

National daily news report (18 Aug 2024): a group of trans women travelling to a protest in Kolkata were subjected to a "gender check" at a metro station, where an in-service railway protection constable allegedly groped one of them to check her gender and made a lewd remark; she filed an FIR; metro and railway protection forces denied the allegations and counter-filed a case against the group; a case was registered under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act. Note: the incident occurred in another state (Kolkata) — documents centralised transit-policing behaviour toward trans travellers nationwide, not this region specifically.
